conclusion-first.title: 結論が先にあるか
conclusion-first.look: The conclusion, the request or the recommendation appears in the first three sentences or the first section. A reader who stops there knows what the document wants.

actionable-ask.title: 頼みごとに、誰が・いつまでにがあるか
actionable-ask.look: Every request says who is to do it and by when. A request missing either is for the writer: the person asked, and the date, are facts only they know.

decision-owner.title: 誰が何を決めるのか分かるか
decision-owner.look: A document asking for a decision names who decides and exactly what is to be decided.

risk-disclosure.title: リスクと、やらなかったときの影響が書かれているか
risk-disclosure.look: A proposal states its risks or drawbacks, and what happens if it is not adopted.

unsourced-number.title: 数字に出どころ・期間・母数があるか
unsourced-number.look: A number that claims an effect or a size (a rise, a cut, a share, a count) says where it comes from, over what period, or out of how many.

unqualified-superlative.title: 「初」「最高」「唯一」に条件が付いているか
unqualified-superlative.look: A superlative (業界初, 最高, 唯一, first, best, only) says within what — the market, the period, the measure.

stacked-hedging.title: ぼかしを重ねていないか
stacked-hedging.look: Two or more hedges on one claim (〜と考えられる可能性があります, 〜かと思われます). The only fix is taking out the extra ones so exactly one remains; the claim stays as certain as the writer made it. A claim with one hedge is fine; any other change to how certain it sounds is the writer's.

agentless-passive.title: 誰がするのかが書かれているか
agentless-passive.look: A passive with no actor (〜が検討されています, 〜が実施される予定です) where the reader needs to know who acts. Naming the actor adds a fact, so it is for the writer.

minutes-sections.title: 決まったことと、やることの一覧があるか
minutes-sections.look: Meeting notes have a part for what was decided and a part for the actions (who does what by when). A heading may be named differently; what matters is that a reader finds both.

proposal-sections.title: 提案に要る部分がそろっているか
proposal-sections.look: A proposal covers the background or problem, the proposal, its expected effect, its cost, its risks, and the next action or the request.

padded-intro.title: 水増しの書き出しになっていないか
padded-intro.look: An opening that could begin any article (近年〜が注目されています, In today's fast-paced world). A sentence that says nothing else may be removed — removed, never replaced with one of your own. One that also carries a fact, or whose removal would leave a heading with nothing under it, is the writer's.

closing-cliche.title: 決まり文句で締めていないか
closing-cliche.look: A stock closing (いかがでしたか, 参考になれば幸いです, In conclusion). A sentence that says nothing else may be removed — removed, never replaced with one of your own. When removing it would leave a heading with nothing under it, it is the writer's.

empty-conclusion.title: 結びが要約だけになっていないか
empty-conclusion.look: The last section only repeats the body, with no judgement, next step or new point. Adding one is the writer's.

title-body-alignment.title: 題が約束したことを本文が扱っているか
title-body-alignment.look: What the title (and the lead, if any) promises is what the body delivers.

thin-section.title: 具体的なもの（数字・例・引用）がない節はないか
thin-section.look: A section with no concrete thing in it — no number, example, code, quotation, link or name. Adding one is the writer's.

duty-owner-deadline.title: 義務に、誰が・いつまでにがあるか
duty-owner-deadline.look: Every obligation or prohibition (〜しなければならない, 〜するものとする, 〜してはならない, shall, must) names who bears it, and, where it has to be done in time, by when. Quote the obligation that lacks one; adding either adds a fact, so it is the writer's.

breach-consequence.title: 守らなかったときどうなるかが書かれているか
breach-consequence.look: An obligation the document relies on says, somewhere in it, what follows when it is not met (解除, 損害賠償, 懲戒, termination, damages). The consequence may stand in another article; what matters is that a reader finds it. Quote the obligation left without one; adding it is the writer's.

exception-with-rule.title: 例外が、決まりのそばにあるか
exception-with-rule.look: An exception to a rule (ただし, 〜を除く, except, unless) stands in the rule's own article, or the rule points to where it is. Quote a rule whose exception a reader could only find by reading the whole document; moving it or pointing to it is the writer's.

scope-stated.title: 誰に、何に当てはまるかが書かれているか
scope-stated.look: A regulation says whom and what it applies to (対象者, 適用範囲), near its start. Quote the opening when it does not; adding it is the writer's.

steps-one-action.title: 手順が、一つずつの動作で番号順に並んでいるか
steps-one-action.look: A procedure is a numbered list with one action per step. Quote a step that asks for two or more actions, or a procedure written as a paragraph; splitting it is the writer's, since the order of the actions is theirs to confirm.

prerequisites-stated.title: 始める前に要るものが書かれているか
prerequisites-stated.look: Before the first step, the procedure says what the reader needs (an account, a permission, a file, a version). Quote the first step when nothing comes before it that a reader needs; adding it is the writer's.

result-check.title: うまくいったことの確かめ方があるか
result-check.look: The procedure says what the reader sees when it worked (a screen, a message, a result), at its end or after a step where it matters. Quote the last step when it does not; adding it is the writer's.

measurable-requirement.title: 満たしたかどうかを確かめられる要件か
measurable-requirement.look: Each requirement says something that can be checked: a number, a limit, a named behaviour. Words that cannot be measured (適切に, 速やかに, 十分な, 高速に, appropriately, promptly, sufficient, fast) leave the reader unable to tell whether it is met. Quote the requirement; the figure or the behaviour is the writer's to supply.

failure-behaviour.title: 失敗や不正な入力のときにどうなるかが書かれているか
failure-behaviour.look: A function, an interface or an operation says what happens when it fails or is given something it cannot take: the message, the code, what is kept or undone. Quote the part that describes only the normal case; the failure behaviour is the writer's to decide.

first-run.title: 最初に動かすまでの手順があるか
first-run.look: A reader who has just found the project can get it running from the document alone: how to install it and the first command to run, in order, with each command written out. Quote where the reader is left to guess; the missing step is the writer's to supply.
